title: rootless: RunUnderSystemdScope waits forever on the StartTransientUnit job channel when the systemd manager never completes the job
body:
### What happened?

Every rootless podman command can hang **forever, with no output and no error**, when the systemd manager never completes the transient-unit job that `RunUnderSystemdScope` waits for.

`RunUnderSystemdScope` ends with:

```go
	ch := make(chan string)
	_, err = conn.StartTransientUnitContext(context.Background(), unitName, "replace", properties, ch)
	if err != nil { ... }

	// Block until job is started
	<-ch

	return nil
```

The `<-ch` read has **no timeout and does not honor the context**. For rootless callers the connection goes to the *user* manager (`cgroups.UserConnection`); if that manager accepts the `StartTransientUnit` call but the job is never removed (wedged user manager, job queued behind a never-completing job, a lost `JobRemoved` signal), the read blocks for eternity. The scope move is best-effort cgroup hygiene on the startup path of **every** rootless podman command (`SetupRootless` → `MovePauseProcessToScope`, and the `euid == 0` branch for the re-exec'd process), so a wedged manager turns into "every rootless podman invocation silently hangs until killed" — and because failures in this helper are only logged at debug level, there is no diagnostic output at all.

This is not hypothetical: on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runners, a rootless `podman info` probe run as a non-login system user (uid 999, linger enabled, cgroup v2 delegation healthy) hung until killed (exit 124) on 11 consecutive CI dispatches, reproducible on every attempt within one runner instance. The podman debug log always ends at

```
time="..." level=info msg="Setting parallel job count to 7"
```

which is printed immediately *before* `SetupRootless` reaches the scope-move path — nothing further is ever printed. (For completeness: in our case the stall finally turned out to be compounded by a separate problem — a lock region left by a different podman version shadowing the distro binary; but the unbounded systemd wait below is real and was separately reproduced.)

A minimal demonstration of the failure class: run any rootless podman command with the user's systemd manager unresponsive (`kill -STOP $(systemctl show -p MainPID --value user@$(id -u).service)`), and the command hangs until externally killed. Pointing `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` / `DBUS_SYSTEM_BUS_ADDRESS` at a dead socket so the connection fails fast makes the hang unreachable — which is how we currently work around it in CI, and rootless containers (pull, build, `podman run --network pasta`) keep working with the scope move degraded, so treating this call as truly best-effort is safe.

### Expected behavior

The wait for the job should be bounded and cancellable — e.g. `select` on the channel, `ctx.Done()` and a timeout — degrading to a debug-logged failure like the other error paths of this helper, instead of wedging the whole command.

### Environment

- Present in podman 5.8.4 via `go.podman.io/common` (`pkg/systemd/systemd_linux.go:104-152` in the vendored module)
- Present in podman 4.9.x (`utils/utils_supported.go:59-60`) — the version shipped in Ubuntu 24.04, where we hit it
- Ubuntu 24.04, cgroup v2, systemd 255, rootless
